assumptions: logical construct sequences and modified-site intent are normally known before MR
strands are typically short and deliberately designed to reduce unintended ambiguity
coordinate chain names, residue numbers and ASU cuts are not construct identity
known_edge_cases: short repeated motifs may still occur
three-nucleotide or other constrained repeats may be unavoidable
single-base sticky ends or overhangs may be intrinsically ambiguous
symmetry-related or equivalent ASU cuts may preserve the same construct
unexpected complete or partial ASU copies may occur

authority_order: explicit reviewed registration or registration recipe
authoritative registration of the actual MR solution

unique whole-chain rename with matching chain length and constant residue-number pattern
unique whole-chain rename plus constant residue-number offset
descriptive design-identity evidence for each simple chain candidate is recorded but not used for assignment
refuse_or_defer: multiple equally valid one-to-one chain assignments
chain-count mismatch suggesting split chains, multiplicity or partial copies

descriptive_design_evidence.caution: Target mismatches can be expected PostMR sequence/modification changes and are not a compatibility score.

sequence_and_modification_policy.future_design_aware_inference: Sequence, modified-site intent, sticky-end definitions and other design information may become explicit evidence in later inference layers when they produce a unique reviewed interpretation. They must not become a hidden composite score.
sequence_and_modification_policy.ambiguity_guard: Repeated short motifs and single-base overhangs must remain capable of producing AMBIGUOUS or guided-review outcomes.

ordinary MR first when a candidate remains plausible
authoritative registration on the actual MR solution before PostMR chemistry
bounded explicit Registration/Recut Rescue only when needed

a split, recut or boundary operation lacks a reviewed recipe
successful MR candidates imply materially different cuts or multiplicities
mapping depends on topology rather than simple construct correspondence

stage_transition_policy.purpose: Describe how registration changes between stages without deciding whether the change is acceptable.
dimensions: single-copy coordinate realization when directly comparable

guided_resolution_v1.scope: simple ambiguous whole-chain Scout candidates only
guided_resolution_v1.input: explicit user selection of logical chain -> coordinate chain
guarantees: selection must cover every logical chain
every selected pair must already be a Scout candidate

guided selection does not use sequence similarity to make the choice
guided selection does not edit coordinates or promote a global recipe

proposed_design_aware_inference_v2.principle: Prefer categorical consistency with declared construct intent over generic sequence-similarity scoring.
candidate_evidence: whether candidate mismatches occur only at sites already declared to change between the family/reference construct and this dataset target
number and identity of unexpected mismatches outside declared-change sites
complete logical-site coverage and one-to-one chain correspondence
proposed_design_aware_inference_v2.suggested_safe_rule: Automatic disambiguation may become eligible only when exactly one complete one-to-one chain mapping has zero unexpected mismatches after accounting for explicitly declared construct-change sites, while every alternative has one or more unexpected mismatches. Otherwise remain AMBIGUOUS.
cautions: do not convert total match count into a weighted score
single-base overhangs and short repeated motifs may remain intrinsically ambiguous
modified-site declarations are intent evidence, not proof of MR correctness
real-data validation is required before promotion into runtime authority

input_evidence: complete simple one-to-one chain assignments from existing length/offset constraints
optional literal residue identities derived from an assessed standard frame-catalogue provider model and bound to existing model-provider provenance
design_aware_scout_v2_experiment.proposal_rule: Propose a mapping only when exactly one complete one-to-one chain mapping has zero unexplained mismatches and every alternative has at least one. Never choose merely because it has fewer unexplained mismatches.
fail_closed: logical chain with no simple candidate
design_aware_scout_v2_experiment.provider_baseline_runtime_requirement: Caller-supplied residue-code dictionaries are no longer accepted. The experimental helper derives provider identities from the exact assessed frame-catalogue model plus NASolve model-provider provenance; runtime promotion remains separately unreviewed.

behavior: accept provider evidence only as provider_assessment plus model_provider provenance
require model-provider selector to match the assessed provider source model
derive residue codes from literal provider coordinates
bind returned provider baseline to source-model SHA-256 and byte size
never accept a caller-supplied site-to-code residue dictionary

surfaces: docs/construct-registration-intent.json machine-readable policy and validation history
active pull request body / branch description
documentation_sync_policy.rule: Keep code/current inference policy and future Topo Net design intent synchronized across active docs. Preserve the separation between input strands, tile hypotheses, periodic crystal graph and ASU serialization; keep project-scoped human validation queues explicit.

future_topo_net_design.invocation_policy: Explicit user/campaign opt-in for designed periodic self-assembling frameworks only; never inferred from coordinates or campaign membership.

ui_relationship.registration_net: General logical-to-coordinate mapping and guided registration view.
ui_relationship.topo_net: Framework-specific extension for periodic molecular-graph visualization and symmetry-aware ASU surgery preview.
ui_relationship.coot: Atomic coordinate materialization and bounded local repair.
ui_relationship.phenix: Post-materialization chemistry/geometry interpretation and refinement audit.

preview_actions: move ASU seam past a residue
move a symmetry-equivalent fragment across the chosen ASU representation
preview newly exposed sticky ends and termini
move a true chemical nick only as an explicitly stronger chemistry-changing operation
open affected coordinates and symmetry mates in Coot

symmetry_bond_experiment.rationale: Phenix supports custom bonds to symmetry copies, but full symmetry-spanning phosphate angle behavior is not yet validated for NASolve. Bond-only enforcement may be insufficient to preserve local phosphate orientation/clash behavior.
minimum_test: use a disposable ordinary DNA PDB with a known representation seam
compare no symmetry bond versus an explicit symmetry-operation P-O3-prime bond
inspect Phenix geometry output and refinement behavior
audit P-O3-prime distance and nearby phosphate/O3-prime nonbonded contacts
do not promote a symmetry-bond policy unless local phosphate geometry is chemically sane and repeatable

coot_seam_rsr_experiment.rationale: Some reslices may leave the intended phosphate/O3-prime connection too long for Phenix to interpret cleanly; bounded single-residue Coot RSR may repair this but must be characterized empirically.
minimum_test: practice on several disposable recut cases
restrict RSR to the intended single residue/local seam
record before/after coordinates for moved atoms
re-run Phenix interpretation and geometry audit
promote only a repeatable bounded operation

validation_goals: reproduce the requested ASU ownership and chain decomposition
show correct sticky ends and representation seams
keep true chemical nicks distinct from representation seams

primary_problem_bias.domain: designed 3-D DNA lattices / periodic nucleic-acid frameworks
primary_problem_bias.strategy: Solve this family well first; generalize later rather than weakening the initial topology semantics with generic crystallographic abstractions.

design_state_layers.meaning: Complete synthesized/declared strands, modifications and intended stoichiometry/copy counts when known.
design_state_layers.caveat: A declared strand may be absent from the solved crystal and observed copy number may disagree with the recipe.

design_state_layers.meaning: Finite design/assembly unit including junctions, sticky ends, true nicks/termini and design-level multiplicity.
Actual repeating molecular connectivity implied by coordinates plus crystallographic symmetry.
One ASU/PDB cut of the periodic graph including chain labels, residue numbering, representation seams and realized tile fragments/copies.

tile_hypothesis_policy.ordinary_case: Use an explicitly declared tile/project design when available.
tile_hypothesis_policy.full_strand_reconstruction: When complete input strands are supplied, they outrank ASU chain fragments as design evidence and may be mapped into the periodic graph under reviewed fail-closed rules.
tile_hypothesis_policy.emergent_case: If the solved periodic graph cannot be represented faithfully by the declared tile, propose an EMERGENT tile hypothesis while retaining the declared tile as experimental intent.
tile_hypothesis_policy.ambiguous_case: If more than one non-equivalent finite tile decomposition survives, remain UNRESOLVED and require expert review.
tile_hypothesis_policy.multiplicity_separation: Tile identity, number of tile copies realized in the ASU, and coordinate-chain decomposition are separate dimensions.
tile_hypothesis_policy.example: A P4_132 ASU containing two complete triangle copies does not redefine the triangle tile; it reports two realized tile copies in that ASU.

input_strand_edge_cases: declared strand absent from observed structure
several copies of one input strand
fewer or more effective tile copies than the input recipe
one input strand split among ASU/symmetry fragments
declared tile inconsistent with observed periodic graph
several non-equivalent tile hypotheses compatible with the evidence
no faithful finite tile decomposition currently known
repeat-bearing/root strand whose designed internal repeat order is not locally commensurate with lattice symmetry
repeat phase that closes only after a long symmetry/unit-cell path
partial use of one repeat-bearing strand
identical repeat units whose phase cannot be uniquely assigned

topo_surgeon.position: Between Topo Net preview/materialization and expert manual Coot fallback.
topo_surgeon.purpose: Repair locally awkward geometry caused by reslicing, mutation, chain reconstruction or imperfect MR coordinates without hiding uncertainty.
candidate_operations: reviewed mutation-before versus mutation-after materialization variants
single-residue Coot RSR at the affected seam
slightly broader local Coot repair only after minimal repair fails
later experimentally validated symmetry-spanning bond policies
audit_dimensions: Phenix local bond/angle geometry and .geo interpretation
topo_surgeon.selection_policy: No hidden composite topology score. Apply reviewed hard gates; preserve surviving alternatives for inspection when necessary.
topo_surgeon.manual_fallback: Open exact model/maps/symmetry seam in Coot for an expert user, then import the saved repaired PDB as a new immutable USER_REVIEWED checkpoint while retaining failed automated attempts.

tile_sequence_sheet.purpose: Preserve real input-strand design intent independently from ASU serialization and observed crystal organization.
per_strand_fields: optional_tile_role such as ROOT/CENTER/ARM/EDGE or project-specific role
tile_sequence_sheet.rule: Intended copies per tile and internal repeat order are separate design dimensions. Neither may be reconstructed from ASU chain counts.

repeat_bearing_strands.rationale: Many designed DNA tiles contain a central/root strand with an internal n-fold repeated role while other strands occur at different copy number. Nature may frustrate or reorganize either the tile stoichiometry or the internal repeat organization.
observed_fields: symmetry/unit-cell path needed for repeat phase to return
repeat_bearing_strands.long_period_semantics: The periodic crystal may advance a repeat-bearing strand through internal phases under symmetry and return to its original phase only after a longer topological closure than the nominal tile. This is not automatically a stoichiometry error.
repeat_bearing_strands.known_style_example: A fivefold repeat-bearing object accommodated in a fourfold/screw lattice may close its repeat phase only after twenty unit-cell steps.
repeat_bearing_strands.partial_use_semantics: A supplied strand may be only partly ordered/incorporated. Preserve exact residue/repeat-domain coverage; do not reduce strand presence to one boolean.

operations: map reviewed repeat domains onto the periodic crystal graph
retain multiple possible repeat-phase correspondences when repeats are indistinguishable
measure whether repeat phase closes locally, over a longer path, or remains unresolved
compare design stoichiometry, repeat usage, coverage and closure as separate facts
forbidden: force designed n-fold repeat order onto the crystal
treat internal repeat count as observed strand copy count
invent missing repeat domains or residues
collapse repeat/stoichiometry disagreement into one compatibility score
repeat_aware_net_finder.backend_note: This can be represented as a repeat-phase/monodromy problem on the periodic graph without exposing that jargon in the user interface.

junction_model.principle: A junction is not defined by arm count. The minimal primitive is one local directed-backbone passage/connection at a topological node; larger four/six/eight-arm neighborhoods are derived context around one or more such primitives.
declaration_fields: one or more minimal backbone-passage primitives
optional observed/contextual arm count and arm identities
optional root/center strand and repeat-domain participation
sticky ends associated with the junction neighborhood
whether the junction is an invariant tile feature under ASU slicing

inference_policy.candidate_generation: periodic connectivity, strand mapping, reviewed pairing/stacking evidence and symmetry may generate hypotheses
inference_policy.automatic_authority: only when uniquely supported under reviewed rules
inference_policy.ambiguous_case: remain CANDIDATE/UNRESOLVED and require expert confirmation
inference_policy.false_positive_case: packing/serialization coincidences may be explicitly REJECTED without changing the periodic graph

junction_model.asu_policy: ASU or tile recutting may change the displayed local arm neighborhood and fragment ownership but must not silently create, destroy or redefine the underlying junction primitive.
junction_model.motivating_semijunction: The topology-based lattice-engineering preprint motivates the minimal primitive: a semi-junction can arise from strand routing/nicking at a crossing and is not ontologically defined by the four-arm neighborhood in which it appears.

persistent_workbench.principle: Keep Topo Net open across surgery, Coot repair, refinement and comparison; every state-changing action creates an immutable checkpoint child.
loop: return metrics and model state to the same Topo session
persistent_workbench.first_refine_behavior: Use a short ordinary audited AutoRefine child from the selected topology checkpoint. Do not introduce selection-restricted Phenix refinement until separately validated.
selected_local_metrics: Phenix bond/angle outliers involving selected residues
reviewed residue/map-fit metrics when a reproducible extractor exists
before/after coordinate displacement for the last operation
persistent_workbench.ui_policy: Keep detailed metrics collapsed until a residue/seam/junction is selected so diagnostics do not consume the topology display.

umbrella_label.meaning: Topology may inform hypotheses, candidate generation, recutting, repair selection, refinement diagnostics and branch comparison, but does not override chemistry, diffraction evidence, fail-closed registration rules or expert review.

generic_model_tree_gui.data_model: Use the existing immutable checkpoint/model lineage; do not create a second GUI-only history.
scope: future re-MR attempts from refined or historical models
interactions: pin/bookmark important historical nodes as comparison panels
inspect metrics for siblings or parent/child nodes without selecting
open a node in Coot without changing the current pointer
select an eligible historical checkpoint using the existing audited selection operation
launch a new explicit branch from an eligible historical node
generic_model_tree_gui.reuse: Standalone normal-mode GUI and Topo Net must share this same graph component and lineage semantics.

future_gui_design.principle: One application shell over authoritative NASolve artifacts and backend operations; no GUI-only scientific state or second lineage system.
future_gui_design.model_lineage: Central immutable stage/checkpoint graph scoped by the selected scientific hierarchy object.

shell.inspector: right contextual metadata and eligible actions
shell.external_atomic_editor: Coot remains the intentional external window

workflow_recipe_product_intent.interaction_rule: GUI may change presentation (buttons/cards/popovers/tree actions) but not eligibility, defaults, provenance or scientific consequence.

construct-registration-intent.json when future contributor/automation continuity depends on the distinction

do not call implementation validated before evidence arrives

scout_naming.rule: Use Scout on scientist-facing CLI/GUI/README/reports. Use v1/v2 only in developer/machine provenance when distinguishing implementation generations or historical validation.
scout_naming.runtime_status: Merged Scout-v2 helper remains proposal-only/non-runtime; public naming does not imply runtime promotion.

collaboration_protocol.principle: Work in coherent slices and exchange a small number of compact multi-command terminal ferries.
ferry_pattern: Complete one coherent code/docs slice before requesting a local run.
Prefer one or a few dense sequential command blocks rather than many tiny commands or multiple alternatives.
Typical ferry order: git pull -> syntax/focused regression -> campaign/family/full regression when warranted -> live action only behind successful && gates -> concise status/worktree.
After returned output, diagnose the first meaningful failure/result before issuing the next ferry.
Promote validation status only after supporting evidence is returned.
documentation_pattern: Material intent changes update the smallest authoritative doc swarm in the same development turn.
README is scientist-facing and contains only current usable behavior.
Developer provenance/history stays in durable dev docs and machine intent.
collaboration_protocol.local_guardrail: Never stage, delete, rename or clean unrelated untracked scientific data, patches, bundles, old environments or example runs without explicit instruction.
